mechanism_narrative: A lower level of the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is associated with higher S&P 500 forward 20-day returns, as lower rates reduce the discount rate for equity valuations.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 4.0%, or the Rank IC for FEDFUNDS as a predictor of 20-day returns is below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3 percentage points over the past month signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which typically leads to reduced corporate profitability and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE rises > 0.3pp in 1 month, or the Rank IC for the UNRATE change signal is below 0.03 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in CPIAUCSL (inflation) and decline in INDPRO (industrial production) indicates stagflationary pressures, prompting central banks to tighten monetary policy and reducing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods where CPIAUCSL increases by >0.2% and INDPRO decreases by >0.5% in the past month, or the Rank IC for the interaction signal is negative over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: During late-cycle economic expansions, a high level of new housing starts (HOUST) indicates robust consumer demand and business investment, which supports corporate earnings growth and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods classified as late-cycle expansion (using standard late-cycle indicators), or the Rank IC for HOUST in late-cycle periods is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A strong consumer spending environment (as measured by RSAFS) is associated with higher corporate revenues and positive S&P 500 forward 5-day returns, as immediate spending trends impact near-term market sentiment.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when RSAFS is above its 1-year moving average, or the Rank IC for RSAFS is below 0.05 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in payroll employment (PAYEMS) by more than 100,000 in the past month signals economic contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 returns as investors anticipate reduced corporate earnings.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where PAYEMS falls > 100k in 1 month, or the Rank IC for PAYEMS change is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in INDPRO (indicating reduced industrial output) and increase in CPIAUCSL (indicating higher inflation) reflects a supply-side shock that pressures corporate margins and prompts central bank tightening, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods where INDPRO falls >0.5% and CPIAUCSL rises >0.2% in the past month, or the Rank IC for the interaction signal is negative over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: In monetary tightening cycles, a robust GDP growth rate (GDPC1) signals economic resilience that mitigates the negative impact of higher interest rates on equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods classified as monetary tightening cycles with GDPC1 above 2.0% annualized, or the Rank IC for GDPC1 in tightening cycles is below 0.05.
